name_en: Sake no yakizuke — grilled salmon steeped in a soy-based sauce
summary_ja: 村上市に伝わる、白焼きにしたサケを酒とみりん、醤油を合わせたたれに漬け込んだ料理。冷凍技術がなかった時代の保存食が起源とされ、冷めても身がふんわりとして固くならないのが特徴と伝わる。
summary_en: A Murakami dish of plain-grilled salmon steeped in a soy-based sauce. Said to have begun as a preservation method before refrigeration existed, it stays soft and tender even after cooling.
source_title: 鮭の焼漬け 新潟県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Namagusa kouko — daikon pickled in a broth of simmered salted sardines
summary_ja: 新潟市角田浜地区に伝わる、塩漬けにしたイワシを煮溶かした汁で大根を漬け込む漬物。地元でとれるイワシを無駄なく使う知恵から生まれたとされ、正月にはどの家庭でも食べられていたと伝わる。
summary_en: A pickle from the Kakudahama district of Niigata City, in which daikon is steeped in a broth made by simmering down salted sardines. Said to have grown from the wisdom of using local sardines without waste, it was reportedly eaten in every household at New Year.
source_title: なまぐさこうこ 新潟県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Fugu no ko no kasuzuke — puffer fish roe cured in salt and sake lees
summary_ja: ゴマフグの卵巣を2年以上塩蔵したのち佐渡の酒粕で長期熟成させる珍味。ふぐ調理師免許を持つ者が処理したものだけが出回り、江戸時代から佐渡でつくられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: A rare Sado delicacy in which puffer fish ovaries are salt-cured for two years or more, then aged for a long stretch in Sado's sake lees. Only ovaries processed by licensed fugu chefs are sold, and the practice is said to date back to the Edo period.
source_title: ふぐの子の粕漬け 新潟県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: 身欠きにしんの糀漬け
name_en: Migaki nishin no kouji-zuke — dried herring pickled with koji and vegetables
summary_ja: 戻した身欠きニシンを大根や白菜と一緒に塩で下漬けし、甘酒で仕上げる阿賀町津川の郷土料理。北前船が運んだ身欠きニシンを内陸で活かす知恵から生まれ、正月のごちそうとして食べられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: A dish from Tsugawa in Agamachi, where rehydrated dried herring is salted with daikon and napa cabbage, then finished with sweet amazake. Born of the inland wisdom for using herring carried in by kitamae-bune ships, it is said to have been served as a New Year treat.
source_title: 身欠きにしんの糀漬け 新潟県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
